purpose: Authoritative-vendor manufacturing integration delta. Adds TrendMiner industrial analytics and Honeywell Uniformance PHD as distinct manufacturing integration targets using existing REST and historian protocol profiles. Records TrendMiner's current early-access MCP capability as a separately gated agent surface, not as a production connector protocol. Evidence remains specification/public-documentation level only: no sandbox or customer tenant credentials were used and all writes remain disabled.

systems.name: TrendMiner
systems.evidenceNote: TrendMiner's current 2026 documentation describes a rich REST API, an in-product API console at /rest-api, and connector APIs for data-source/provider discovery, tag enumeration and indexed time-series reads. The platform can sit over historians and industrial sources including AVEVA PI, AspenTech IP.21, GE Proficy, Yokogawa Exaquantum, Honeywell PHD, Canary, AWS IoT SiteWise and generic database/file sources. Current 2026 innovation documentation also describes an early-access MCP Server with tools for tag/asset discovery, tag data, value-based search and analytics; because the early-access toolset also includes add_calculations, MCP is treated as a separately gated agent/management surface rather than a normal WFM read protocol. No TrendMiner tenant or MCP environment was authenticated.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised TrendMiner identity limited to the tags, assets, analyses and contexts needed by WFM
read-only REST operations for tag/asset discovery and analytical/time-series results
no ConfigHub, connector configuration, calculation creation, user/role administration or other mutative permission during discovery
on self-hosted deployments, access only through the customer-approved HTTPS/edge/network path
MCP tool discovery or read tools only if an authorised Early Access environment proves operation-level permissions and auditability
dataAvailableOrExpected: industrial tags and indexed time-series data
tag types, metadata and historian/data-source identity
asset hierarchy and contextual information where configured
calculated, searched and analytical results created in TrendMiner
historian/provider inventory through the customer's configured Plant Integrations layer
context data from supported enterprise/industrial sources where licensed and configured
automationOpportunities: use customer-approved TrendMiner operating-state, anomaly and downtime analytics to refine labour demand and redeployment recommendations
correlate staffing, throughput and downtime across multiple historians through one governed analytics layer
reuse TrendMiner's existing historian/provider mappings instead of creating duplicate direct plant integrations
preserve interpolation type and query interval metadata so sampled analytical data is not mistaken for raw telemetry
detect changed tags, providers, asset mappings and API behaviour after TrendMiner upgrades before decisions are affected
evaluate MCP read tools for implementation/support acceleration only after separate agent-security proof; keep add_calculations and other mutations disabled
savingsHypotheses: reduce duplicate historian integration engineering by consuming TrendMiner's governed industrial analytics layer
reduce paid idle labour by acting on sustained downtime/recovery analytics rather than isolated tag changes
reduce manual root-cause and shift analysis by joining WFM outcomes to TrendMiner analytics
reduce implementation effort for estates containing mixed historians and legacy data providers
if the MCP read surface is later certified, reduce AI/agent integration effort by reusing vendor-supported discovery and data tools
dataGaps: worker, payroll, qualification and roster truth normally remains outside TrendMiner
tag names, asset hierarchy, calculations and contextual models are customer-specific
TrendMiner may interpolate or index source values; exact raw-versus-derived semantics must be retained
provider availability and supported versions differ by TrendMiner release and customer deployment
MCP is early access and does not yet establish a production-safe least-privilege WFM contract
constraintsRisks: the REST API supports mutative methods as well as GET, so operation allowlists and least-privilege roles are mandatory
self-hosted TrendMiner and Plant Integrations can be close to historians and may use firewall-unfriendly legacy drivers; WFM must not bypass the customer edge
indexed reads explicitly use interpolation types and intervals, which must be carried into lineage/quality metadata
large tag/time ranges require bounded windows and controlled concurrency
upgrades can change API details; current 2026 upgrade guidance warns stricter trailing-slash handling can break existing integrations
MCP currently includes add_calculations and may gain more tools; tool names or inherited user permissions are not evidence of safe read-only authority
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST profile for a thin TrendMiner adapter with version/capability discovery, read-operation allowlists, bounded time-series windows, explicit interpolation/index metadata, source-historian lineage, tag/asset schema fingerprints and customer work-centre mappings. Treat self-hosted endpoints as customer-network resources and never connect directly to underlying historians through WFM cloud. Separately model TrendMiner MCP only after an authorised Early Access environment proves tool enumeration, read-only filtering, identity/audit boundaries and safe failure behaviour. Then obtain an authorised TrendMiner tenant for least-privilege authentication and a read round-trip.

systems.name: Honeywell Uniformance Process History Database (PHD)
systems.evidenceNote: Honeywell describes Uniformance PHD as its process historian for collecting, storing and replaying historical and continuous plant process data. Honeywell's PHD API guidance deprecates VisualPHD/ModTag for new software and identifies supported alternatives including PHDAPINet, OLEDB, ODBC, Java API, OPC DA/HDA, OPC UA and a RESTful API. Manufacturing WFM records only reusable REST, OPC UA and ODBC-family routes and does not rely on deprecated VisualPHD or create a new vendor-specific transport. A 2026 Honeywell lifecycle publication continues to list PHD as an active Enterprise Data Management product. No customer PHD environment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised read identity limited to approved PHD tags/history and asset areas
REST or ODBC read access where available, or OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe only through a customer-edge gateway
no tag modification, manual-input, archive administration, historian configuration or process/control writes
customer site/network and historian security controls remain authoritative
no deprecated VisualPHD/ModTag dependency for new connector work
dataAvailableOrExpected: historical and continuous plant process tag values
tag definitions, engineering units and historian metadata where exposed by the selected API
event/journal context where the customer's PHD configuration exposes it
asset/process context mapped by the customer's historian implementation
automationOpportunities: use historical machine/process state to improve staffing demand, downtime response and labour redeployment recommendations
correlate staffing and overtime with process throughput, recurring stoppages and recovery patterns
use historian evidence to coordinate maintenance windows and specialist skill demand
reuse a long-lived PHD estate rather than require customers to modernise historians before adopting WFM
detect tag/schema/version drift and API-path deprecation before historian changes affect WFM decisions
consider any write or manual-input route only after a separate authorised sandbox/site write safety case
savingsHypotheses: reduce integration cost by reusing existing PHD estates and standard read interfaces
reduce paid idle labour by identifying process stoppage/recovery patterns by shift
reduce emergency maintenance overtime through better historical failure/condition correlation
extend workforce optimisation to legacy sites that cannot immediately migrate their historian
dataGaps: PHD tag naming, hierarchy, event models and asset semantics are customer-specific
worker identity, schedule, payroll and qualification data usually come from separate enterprise systems
exact REST endpoint/version/authentication documentation is distributed with the customer's PHD software and therefore must be verified per deployed release
calculated/virtual tags must be distinguished from raw measurements
older estates may expose deprecated or legacy interfaces that should not be selected for new work
constraintsRisks: PHD deployments are commonly on-prem and plant-network adjacent; direct cloud access is prohibited and customer-edge routing is required
legacy API availability varies by PHD release; VisualPHD and ModTag are deprecated for new software
OPC UA and ODBC permissions must be read-only and bounded to required tags/data sets
large historical queries require bounded windows, backpressure and deterministic checkpoints
timestamps, quality and calculated/virtual-tag provenance must be preserved before using historian values for real-time WFM actions
customer upgrade/support matrices determine compatible API options and should be captured during implementation
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST, OPC UA and database-read profiles for a thin Uniformance PHD adapter; explicitly reject deprecated VisualPHD/ModTag for new builds. Add deployed-version/API capability discovery, customer-edge enforcement, read-only tag namespace mapping, bounded history reads, quality/source-time/provenance preservation, schema/tag fingerprints and customer asset/work-centre mappings. Obtain customer-version API documentation plus an authorised PHD lab or tenant for least-privilege authentication and read round-trip proof before considering any write path.
